rv.q: What shocks in the end is that a play — yes, a play — that can, through its 80-minute running time, seem to de-prioritize plot for the poetic, also can conclude with an emotional wallop only a great playwright could produce, and only a stone could ignore.
Sarah Ruhl’s play has aged well and it’s exciting to see one of her earlier works done to such incredible standards at a theater not far from where she grew up.
Bizarre as all these characters are, and how strange their circumstances, all is gloriously humorous.
It was sad and memorable, in part funny and hopeful and so was a successful production.
This season opener, a modern version of a familiar myth, while inventive, imaginative and enticing is, in the end, just a little disappointing and a bit perplexing for most audiences.
The cast of players is sheer perfection.
The production is Eurydice at its best; it plays out on stage exactly as it reads on the page.

cn.t: Critics praise this visually exquisite production of Sarah Ruhl's reimagined Greek myth, celebrating its whimsical dialogue, childlike wonder, and poetic staging that creates an innovative and emotionally resonant evening of theater.
